expl.summary: Each jet (its 8 hardest particles) is placed on 16 neurons, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables, and each of the five class scores adds some neurons and subtracts others; this smaller formula (399 terms, step 4 of the formula tuned on the network) reaches an accuracy of 0.653 on the validation jets. The t score is built mainly on λ₁+λ₂: it subtracts neuron 13 (ΣzΔR below 0.148 and λ₁ below 0.0161; true tops average 1.09 on it, every other class 3.6-4.5; -48% of the t score) and adds neuron 10 (overall λ₁+λ₂: ΣzΔR, ΣzΔR², λ₁; +26%), so it follows ΣzΔR and λ₁+λ₂ with rank correlations of 0.915 and 0.912. The q score is mostly neuron 9 (narrow, centred jets, +56%) minus neuron 10 (λ₁+λ₂, -18%), and follows jet mass and λ₁+λ₂ downwards (rank correlations -0.768 and -0.766). The g score also adds neuron 9 (+22%), and in addition the low-mass, low-angularity neuron 2 (+38%, its largest input) and the broad, high-pT neuron 1 (+13%); it subtracts neuron 5 (pT concentrated in the hardest particles, -14%), which is how gluons are separated from quarks. The two boson scores share the elongated neuron 7 (+13% of W, +36% of Z) and subtract wide-angle radiation (neuron 3: -16% of W, -23% of Z) and the broad, off-centre neuron 6 (-9% and -14%). They are split mainly by λ₁+λ₂: the W score adds the compact, centred neuron 11 (+23%) and neuron 0 (+10%), which the Z score does not use, and subtracts the intermediate-λ₁+λ₂ neuron 14 (-9%) and the moderate-λ₁+λ₂ neuron 15 (-7%), while the Z score adds neuron 14 (+6%). One offered particle-mass threshold is used: mass > 91.2 GeV (the Z mass) in neuron 12, which does not enter any class score; since the jet mass here is that of the 8 hardest particles and does not peak at the W, Z or top masses, it acts as an ordinary cut on large mass.
